source_node.label: Oculus Browser Remote UI HTML Injection and Potential Code Execution
source_node.precondition: User visits an attacker-controlled remote web page using Oculus Browser versions 5.2.7 through 5.7.11.
source_node.postcondition: Injection of arbitrary HTML into the Oculus Browser UI, enabling UI spoofing and arbitrary code execution in the context of the browser process.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRServiceLauncher.exe Process Handle Leak Privilege Escalation
target_node.precondition: Local low-privilege process execution on Windows host running Oculus Desktop > 1.39 and < 31.1.0.67.507.
target_node.postcondition: Acquisition of a leaked privileged process handle from OVRServiceLauncher.exe, leading to local privilege escalation.

offline.claim: Initial code execution via browser vulnerability provides the unprivileged process needed to capture the leaked privileged handle.

source.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

applicability_rule.note: 'potentially execute code': user-level foothold is the generous reading. Requires the victim to open an attacker-controlled page (inferred from 'remote web page').
applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

target.description: Due to a bug with management of handles in OVRServiceLauncher.exe, an attacker could expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation. This issue affects Oculus Desktop versions after 1.39 and prior to 31.1.0.67.507.

applicability_rule.warning: E1 effect levels are not guaranteed CVE postconditions

response.reason: CVE-2019-3562 directly describes arbitrary HTML injection into the Oculus Browser UI and only potentially executing code. CVE-2021-24038 describes a handle-management bug that could expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation. A bounded causal bridge is therefore possible only if the browser issue actually yields suitable local unprivileged-process execution on the same relevant host and that process can interact with the vulnerable Oculus Desktop service. The supplied descriptions and absent environment observations do not establish those conditions, and the claim that initial browser execution provides the needed process and captures the handle overreaches the evidence. This is conditional and should not enter a strict graph as a confirmed edge.
